
Various normal distributions are shown in the visualisation below, for different values of\ $\mu$ and\ $\sigma$.
For the same value of\ $\mu$, larger values of\ $\sigma$ show more variation in teh distribution (as expected).



```{r, NormalDemo, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center", fig.cap="Normal distributions."}
library(plotly)

# Parameters
mus    <- c(0, 3)
sigmas <- c(1, 2)

x <- seq(-5, 10, length.out = 600)

fig <- plot_ly(width = 650, height = 450)

# --- create all traces ---
library(plotly)

# --- Parameters ---
mus    <- c(0, 3)
sigmas <- c(1, 2)

x <- seq(-5, 10, length.out = 600)

# Compute axis ranges
xrange <- c(-5, 10)
yrange <- c(0, max(1/(sigmas * sqrt(2*pi))) * 1.05)  # max PDF across all σ

# --- Create figure and all traces ---
fig <- plot_ly(width = 650, height = 450)

counter <- 1
for(m in mus){
  for(s in sigmas){
    fig <- fig %>% add_lines(
      x = x,
      y = dnorm(x, mean = m, sd = s),
      visible = FALSE,
      line = list(color = "steelblue", width = 2.5),
      name = paste0("μ=", m, ", σ=", s),
      showlegend = FALSE
    )
    counter <- counter + 1
  }
}

# Make default trace visible (μ=0, σ=1)
# Make only μ=0 σ=1 visible initially
for(i in seq_along(fig$x$data)) {
  trace <- fig$x$data[[i]]
  if(trace$name == "μ=0, σ=1") {
    fig$x$data[[i]]$visible <- TRUE
  } else {
    fig$x$data[[i]]$visible <- FALSE
  }
}

# --- Build 2x2 buttons ---
buttons <- list()
counter <- 1
for(m in mus){
  for(s in sigmas){
    vis <- rep(FALSE, length(mus)*length(sigmas))
    vis[counter] <- TRUE
    
    buttons[[counter]] <- list(
      method = "update",
      args = list(
        list(visible = vis),
        list(
          title = paste0("Normal PDF: μ=", m, ", σ=", s),
          xaxis = list(range = xrange),
          yaxis = list(range = yrange)
        )
      ),
      label = paste0("μ=", m, ", σ=", s)
    )
    
    counter <- counter + 1
  }
}

# --- Layout with 2x2 grid of buttons ---
top_row_buttons    <- buttons[1:2]  # μ=0
bottom_row_buttons <- buttons[3:4]  # μ=3

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = list(text = "Normal distribution", x = 0.5),
  xaxis = list(title = "x", range = xrange),
  yaxis = list(title = "Density", range = yrange),
updatemenus = list(
  list(
    type = "buttons",
    direction = "right",
    x = 0,
    y = -0.2,
    xanchor = "left",
    yanchor = "top",
    buttons = top_row_buttons
  ),
  list(
    type = "buttons",
    direction = "right",
    x = 0,
    y = -0.3,
    xanchor = "left",
    yanchor = "top",
    buttons = bottom_row_buttons
  )
))

# Display plot
fig
```
